title: Calculate CPPS with Optimized Single-Call (Tier 4 Ultra) — calculate_cpps_ultra
text: Implements complete CPPS pipeline one C++ call, following approach used AVQI v2.03 v3.01: PowerCepstrogram creation CPPS extraction consolidated, intermediate R object allocated. **** make meaningfully cheaper CPPS entry points: per-frame robust trend fit (`SlopeSelector::getSlope_Siegel`) dominates CPPS runtime shared every path; consolidating PowerCepstrogram creation removes R/C++ boundary crossing, small fraction total cost. Treat choice matter call-site convenience, performance. defaults match calculate_cpps_fast() therefore also deviate Praat's dialog defaults — see "Defaults differ Praat's" section calculate_cpps_fast. still **CPPS** helper. single-interval **CPP** measurement, use segment's `Spectrum -> PowerCepstrum -> get_peak_prominence()` path instead `calculate_cpps_ultra()`. cheaper closer Praat workflow used voice-quality scripts query one interval time. **Use Cases:** - AVQI v2.03/v3.01 implementation - High-throughput voice quality analysis - CPPS monitoring latency-sensitive pipelines

title: Check Audio Quality Metrics — check_audio_quality
text: function designed catch common recording problems: **Clipping Detection**: Identifies signal exceeds threshold (default 0.99). Clipped recordings distorted peaks typically re-recorded. **Intensity Analysis**: Uses Praat's intensity measurement assess signal strength. low mean intensity may indicate recording level problems. **Dynamic Range**: difference maximum minimum intensity can help identify recordings poor signal--noise ratio excessive compression. **Quality Criteria** (general guidelines): - clipping (is_clipped = FALSE) - Mean intensity: -20 -10 dB speech - Dynamic range: > 20 dB - Max amplitude: 0.7-0.9 range (good headroom without clipping)

title: Extract Voiced Segments with AVQI Filtering (Tier 4 Ultra) — extract_voiced_segments_ultra
text: **TIER 4 ULTRA API** function implements exact AVQI voiced extraction algorithm single C++ call. replaces R loops multiple boundary crossings standard multi-step approach. **Algorithm (AVQI v3.01):** 1. Detect silences using intensity-based TextGrid creation 2. Extract "sounding" intervals 3. Concatenate sounding intervals -> "loud_sound" 4. Slide 30ms windows loud_sound 5. Filter windows : power > 30 6. Concatenate passing windows -> final voiced sound **Algorithm (AVQI v2.03):** Steps 1-3 (window filtering) **Version Differences:** - v2.03: Simpler, keeps voiced content (~37s 37s input) - v3.01: Aggressive ZCR filtering, removes fricatives (~25-30s 37s input)

title: Extract Voiced Segments with AVQI Filtering (Tier 4 Ultra) — extract_voiced_segments_ultra
text: pitch algorithm used — voiced/silence segmentation Intensity-threshold based (`Sound_to_Intensity()` + `silence_threshold_db` relative maximum), derived `Pitch` object. `min_pitch` controls Intensity analysis window length (via `Sound_to_Intensity`'s floor parameter), pitch-detection algorithm choice. See Tier 4 Ultra algorithm table `inst/agents/AGENT_GUIDE.md`.

what: Get All Jitter and Shimmer Measures in One Call — get_jitter_shimmer_batch
title: Get All Jitter and Shimmer Measures in One Call — get_jitter_shimmer_batch
text: Returns 11 voice quality measures (5 jitter, 6 shimmer) single C++ call, instead calling individual methods separately measure. **Jitter measures** (period perturbation): - `jitter_local`: Local jitter (relative, fraction) - `jitter_local_abs`: Local absolute jitter (seconds) - `jitter_rap`: Relative average perturbation - `jitter_ppq5`: 5-point period perturbation quotient - `jitter_ddp`: Difference differences periods **Shimmer measures** (amplitude perturbation): - `shimmer_local`: Local shimmer (relative, fraction) - `shimmer_local_db`: Local shimmer (dB) - `shimmer_apq3`: 3-point amplitude perturbation quotient - `shimmer_apq5`: 5-point amplitude perturbation quotient - `shimmer_apq11`: 11-point amplitude perturbation quotient - `shimmer_dda`: Difference differences amplitudes

what: Get Voice Quality Metrics in Single Call (Tier 4 Ultra) — get_voice_quality_ultra
title: Get Voice Quality Metrics in Single Call (Tier 4 Ultra) — get_voice_quality_ultra
text: Complete voice quality pipeline C++: Sound -> Pitch -> PointProcess -> Jitter/Shimmer/HNR metrics, one call instead equivalent Tier 2/3 workflow using separate function calls. **Tier 4 "Ultra"** function batch DSI (Dysphonia Severity Index) calculations jitter PPQ5 PPQ component. default, keeps existing Tier 4 pitch path (`pitch_method = "cc"`, `very_accurate = TRUE`). reference workflow uses Praat's plain `Pitch...` command `PointProcess (cc)` (example DSI jitter block), call `pitch_method = "ac", very_accurate = FALSE` — equivalent shorthand `pitch_method = "periodic_cc"` (see ).

title: Get Voice Quality Metrics in Single Call (Tier 4 Ultra) — get_voice_quality_ultra
code: get_voice_quality_ultra(   sound,   metrics = "all",   min_pitch = 75,   max_pitch = 600,   time_step = 0,   pitch_method = c("cc", "ac", "periodic_cc"),   very_accurate = TRUE )

title: Get Voice Quality Metrics in Single Call (Tier 4 Ultra) — get_voice_quality_ultra
text: sound Sound object metrics Character vector metrics compute: "jitter", "shimmer", "hnr", "" metrics min_pitch Pitch floor Hz pitch extraction (default: 75). Note: HNR always uses 75 Hz minimum pitch (Praat's CC harmonicity default), independent parameter. max_pitch Pitch ceiling Hz (default: 600) time_step Time step pitch/HNR (0 = auto; HNR auto uses 0.01 s) pitch_method Pitch algorithm jitter/shimmer pitch object: `"cc"` (default, preserves existing Tier 4 behaviour), `"ac"`, `"periodic_cc"` — alias `"ac"` `very_accurate` forced `FALSE`, matching Praat's `PointProcess (periodic, cc)...` command (see Algorithm choice section ). very_accurate Logical; whether use Praat's accurate pitch path jitter/shimmer pitch extraction (default: `TRUE` preserve existing Tier 4 output). Use `FALSE` `pitch_method = "ac"` match Praat's plain `Pitch...` command. Ignored (forced `FALSE`) `pitch_method = "periodic_cc"`.

title: Get Voice Quality Metrics in Single Call (Tier 4 Ultra) — get_voice_quality_ultra
text: Named list requested voice quality metrics: jitter_local Local jitter (relative, fraction) jitter_local_abs Local absolute jitter (seconds) jitter_rap Relative average perturbation jitter_ppq5 5-point period perturbation quotient (DSI PPQ component) jitter_ddp Difference differences periods shimmer_local Local shimmer (relative, fraction) shimmer_local_db Local shimmer (dB) shimmer_apq3 3-point amplitude perturbation quotient shimmer_apq5 5-point amplitude perturbation quotient shimmer_apq11 11-point amplitude perturbation quotient shimmer_dda Difference differences amplitudes hnr_mean Mean harmonics--noise ratio (dB) hnr_sd Standard deviation HNR

title: Get Voice Quality Metrics in Single Call (Tier 4 Ultra) — get_voice_quality_ultra
text: Praat's `Sound: PointProcess (periodic, cc)...` command , per Praat's source (`Sound_to_PointProcess.cpp`) manual, exactly `Sound_to_Pitch(sound, 0, floor, ceiling)` (.e. `Sound_to_Pitch_rawAc` `veryAccurate = FALSE` Praat's raw defaults `0.03, 0.45, 0.01, 0.35, 0.14`) followed `Sound_Pitch_to_PointProcess_cc`. byte--byte function already computes called `pitch_method = "ac", very_accurate = FALSE`. `pitch_method = "periodic_cc"` pure alias combination (forces `very_accurate = FALSE` regardless `very_accurate` argument), callers porting Praat script uses `PointProcess (periodic, cc)...` can request matching Tier 4 path name instead know two equivalent.

title: Get Voice Quality Metrics in Single Call (Tier 4 Ultra) — get_voice_quality_ultra
text: **Tier 4 "Ultra"** function. entire workflow (pitch extraction, PointProcess creation, voice quality calculations) happens C++ intermediate R objects.

title: Get Voice Quality Metrics in Single Call (Tier 4 Ultra) — get_voice_quality_ultra
code: sound <- Sound$create_tone(frequency = 150, duration = 0.5, sampling_rate = 16000)  # Get all voice quality metrics vq <- get_voice_quality_ultra(sound, metrics = "all", min_pitch = 75)  # Get only jitter metrics (DSI PPQ component) vq <- get_voice_quality_ultra(sound, metrics = "jitter") ppq5 <- vq$jitter_ppq5  # Match a plain pitch extraction + PointProcess (cc) DSI path vq_ac <- get_voice_quality_ultra(   sound,   metrics = "jitter",   pitch_method = "ac",   very_accurate = FALSE )  # Equivalent shorthand for the periodic-cc PointProcess path vq_periodic_cc <- get_voice_quality_ultra(   sound,   metrics = "jitter",   pitch_method = "periodic_cc" )

title: pladdrr: Direct Access to Praat C Functionality from R — pladdrr-package
text: pladdrr package provides direct access Praat's C phonetic analysis functionality R. Praat widely-used tool speech analysis phonetics research package wraps Praat's core C library using Rcpp, providing native access Praat's analysis capabilities without requiring external Praat installation scripting.

title: pladdrr: Direct Access to Praat C Functionality from R — pladdrr-package
text: Sound Operations: Create manipulate sound objects Read write audio files (WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3, NIST via native Praat) Extract basic sound properties (duration, sampling rate, etc.) Generate synthetic sounds (sine waves, white noise) Pitch Analysis: Extract fundamental frequency (F0) contours Get pitch specific time points Calculate pitch statistics (mean, median, range) Quality-aware pitch tracking configurable parameters Formant Analysis: Extract formant frequencies (F1-F5) Get formants specific time points Calculate formant statistics trajectories LPC-based formant estimation Intensity Spectral Analysis: Compute intensity contours Create spectrograms Extract spectral properties

title: pladdrr: Direct Access to Praat C Functionality from R — pladdrr-package
text: pladdrr package follows core principles: Scientific Accuracy: analyses must match Praat's output         within 0.1% relative error tolerance R Package Standards: Full compliance CRAN requirements         R package best practices Direct C++ Integration: Direct C++ access via Rcpp, avoiding         intermediate R-level translation layers Test-Driven Development: Comprehensive test coverage         reference validation Comprehensive Documentation: functions fully documented         examples vignettes

title: pladdrr: Direct Access to Praat C Functionality from R — pladdrr-package

title: Control multi-threading of Praat analyses — pladdrr_threads
text: package's batch helpers (`analyze_files_parallel()`, `process_sounds_parallel()`, `batch_process()`) already cap worker's threads automatically, need running parallel loop (e.g. hand-written `mclapply()` worker stay single-threaded). Threading never changes results: threads partition analysis frames frame computed exactly single-threaded mode.

Available window shapes (see Praat manual details): - "rectangular" (default) - tapering - "triangular" - Triangular (Bartlett) taper - "parabolic" - Parabolic (Welch) taper - "hanning" - Hanning window - "hamming" - Hamming window - "gaussian1" - Gaussian window (sd=0.42466) - "gaussian2" - Narrower Gaussian (sd=0.21233), use relative_width=2.0 - "gaussian3" - Even narrower (sd=0.14155), use relative_width=3.0 - "gaussian4" - narrow (sd=0.10616), use relative_width=4.0 - "gaussian5" - Extremely narrow (sd=0.08493), use relative_width=5.0 - "kaiser1" - Kaiser-Bessel window (alpha=20.7) - "kaiser2" - Narrower Kaiser-Bessel (alpha=40.5), use relative_width=2.0

Channel analyze stereo (default: 1) avqi_compatible Logical. Use AVQI-compatible analysis window (0.0025-0.0275s within frame) instead full frame (default: TRUE)

title: Calculate Zero Crossing Rate for Sound — sound_get_zcr
text: Named list :   - `times`: Numeric vector frame center times   - `zcr`: Numeric vector zero crossing rates (crossings per second)   - `window_duration`: Window duration used   - `hop_duration`: Hop duration used

title: Calculate Zero Crossing Rate for Sound — sound_get_zcr
text: Uses Praat's `to_point_process_zeros()` accurate zero crossing detection interpolation. `avqi_compatible = TRUE` (default), uses AVQI203.praat's checkZeros procedure: analyzes zeros within 0.0025-0.0275s frame (25ms analysis window within 30ms frame). matches Praat's AVQI implementation. Typical ZCR values: - Voiced speech: 500-2000 crossings/second - Unvoiced speech: 3000-6000 crossings/second - Silence: variable, depends noise AVQI, segments ZCR > 3000 Hz typically rejected unvoiced.

title: Load Sound Window from File with Optional Resampling — sound_load_window
text: traditional workflow loads entire file, resamples entire file, extracts window interest — reading processing far samples needed. function instead opens file `LongSound` (lazily, reading header), extracts just requested window disk, resamples window. **Use cases:** - Pharyngeal analysis: extracting short vowel windows long recordings - Formant tracking: analyzing specific time points - Batch extraction: processing windows multiple files - Large file processing: working hours-long recordings

title: Load Sound Window from File with Optional Resampling — sound_load_window
code: # Write a short synthetic recording, then load only part of it sound <- Sound$create_tone(frequency = 220, duration = 2.0) path <- tempfile(fileext = ".wav") sound$save(path)  window <- sound_load_window(path, start = 0.5, end = 0.6)  # Extract and resample (for spectral analysis) window_10k <- sound_load_window(path, start = 0.5, end = 0.6, resample_to = 10000)  # Preserve original time domain (window starts at 0.5, not 0.0) window_timed <- sound_load_window(path, start = 0.5, end = 0.6, preserve_times = TRUE)  unlink(path)

title: Merge Multiple TextGrid Objects — textgrid_merge
text: TextGrid object (external pointer)

title: Merge Multiple TextGrid Objects — textgrid_merge
text: Manual merge requires save/reload plus O(n²) sequence `insert_boundary` calls (insert shifts later intervals); batch merge single O(n) pass proper interval handling. **Domain handling:** - `equalize_domains = FALSE` (default):   * New domain runs min(xmin) max(xmax) input TextGrids   * Tiers retain original domains - `equalize_domains = TRUE`:   * tiers extended new domain   * Empty intervals added edges needed **Use cases:** - VUV analysis: Merging original TextGrid VUV tier - Multi-annotator: Combining annotations different annotators - Workflow: Adding automatic tiers manual annotations

title: Merge Multiple TextGrid Objects — textgrid_merge
code: # Create test TextGrids tg1 <- textgrid_create(0, 1, "words") tg1$insert_boundary(1, 0.5) tg1$set_interval_text(1, 1, "hello") tg1$set_interval_text(1, 2, "world")  tg2 <- textgrid_create(0, 1, "events", "events") tg2$insert_point(1, 0.25, "click")  # Batch merge merged <- textgrid_merge(list(tg1, tg2)) # Result has 2 tiers: "words" (interval) + "events" (point)  # With domain equalization merged_eq <- textgrid_merge(list(tg1, tg2), equalize_domains = TRUE)
